quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write a friendly email introducing yourself to a new classmate.
options: SUBJECT: HI FROM YOUR NEW CLASSMATE
MY NAME IS ALEX AND I JUST JOINED YOUR CLASS - I HOPE WE GET TO KNOW EACH OTHER AND BECOME GOOD FRIENDS.

BEST WISHES,
ALEX
DEAR ZOE,
quests.hint: The self-introduction purpose is in the subject; 'DEAR ZOE' opens warmly; the introduction and hope for friendship are in the body; 'BEST WISHES' closes politely.
quests.explanation: Even casual emails benefit from a clear structure. Writing to a new classmate sits between formal and informal - 'Dear' and 'Best wishes' are polite but not overly formal for a peer.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write an email to a music school asking about piano lessons.
options: SUBJECT: ENQUIRY ABOUT PIANO LESSONS FOR A TEENAGER
DEAR MUSIC SCHOOL OFFICE,

KIND REGARDS,
OLIVER MARSH
I AM FOURTEEN YEARS OLD AND WOULD LIKE TO KNOW WHETHER YOU OFFER INDIVIDUAL PIANO LESSONS AND WHAT THE TERM FEES ARE.
quests.hint: The instrument, lesson type, and age are in the subject; the school office is addressed by role, not name; two questions form the body; 'KIND REGARDS' closes politely.
quests.explanation: 'Kind regards' fits an enquiry to a general office better than 'Yours sincerely', which should be kept for emails to a named person. Always ask about both availability AND cost to get a complete picture.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write an email thanking a friend for giving you career advice.
options: I REALLY APPRECIATED THE TIME YOU TOOK TO TALK THROUGH MY CAREER OPTIONS WITH ME - YOUR ADVICE HAS GIVEN ME GREAT CLARITY.

WITH WARM WISHES,
BEN
SUBJECT: THANK YOU FOR YOUR WONDERFUL CAREER ADVICE
DEAR CAROLINE,
quests.hint: 'DEAR CAROLINE' opens warmly but respectfully; the appreciation and outcome are in the body; 'WITH WARM WISHES' closes sincerely; the subject captures the theme.
quests.explanation: 'With warm wishes' is a slightly more personal variant of 'Warm regards' and works well when you want to convey genuine gratitude. Mentioning the positive outcome ('great clarity') makes the thanks more meaningful.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write an email to a library asking about membership for adults.
options: DEAR LIBRARY TEAM,

MANY THANKS,
GRACE FORD
SUBJECT: ENQUIRY ABOUT ADULT LIBRARY MEMBERSHIP
I WOULD LIKE TO JOIN THE LIBRARY AND WONDER IF YOU COULD TELL ME WHAT I NEED TO BRING TO REGISTER AS AN ADULT MEMBER.
quests.hint: The membership purpose and age group are in the subject; the team is addressed professionally; the practical question is in the body; 'MANY THANKS' closes politely.
quests.explanation: Asking what you need to bring in advance saves an unnecessary trip. 'Many thanks' is a friendly closing well-suited to public service enquiries like library membership.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write an email inviting a cousin on a day trip to the seaside.
options: HI CHARLIE,
I AM PLANNING A DAY TRIP TO WHITBY NEXT SATURDAY AND WAS WONDERING IF YOU WOULD LIKE TO COME ALONG FOR THE ADVENTURE.
SUBJECT: DAY TRIP TO THE SEASIDE - INTERESTED?

CAN'T WAIT,
MIA
quests.hint: 'HI CHARLIE' is a casual cousin greeting; 'CAN'T WAIT' is an enthusiastic, informal closing; the invitation details are in the body; the subject question creates excitement.
quests.explanation: Casual trip invitations can use energetic closings like 'Can't wait!' which reflects genuine excitement. Adding the destination name ('Whitby') makes the invitation more concrete and appealing.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write an email to a colleague who is off sick wishing them a speedy recovery.
options:
WARMLY,
THE ACCOUNTS TEAM
SUBJECT: GET WELL SOON - WE ARE THINKING OF YOU
WE ARE ALL SORRY TO HEAR YOU ARE UNWELL AND HOPE YOU MAKE A SPEEDY RECOVERY - PLEASE DON'T WORRY ABOUT WORK.
DEAR ANNA,
quests.hint: The caring message is in the subject; 'DEAR ANNA' is a warm professional greeting; reassurance and well-wishes are in the body; 'WARMLY' closes with genuine human warmth.
quests.explanation: Signing off from a team ('The Accounts Team') is appropriate when writing on behalf of a group. Telling someone 'don't worry about work' removes a significant source of stress during illness.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write an email asking a community centre about when the photography club meets.
options:
KIND REGARDS,
RAY HOLLOWAY
SUBJECT: QUESTION ABOUT THE PHOTOGRAPHY CLUB MEETING TIMES
DEAR COMMUNITY CENTRE MANAGER,
I AM INTERESTED IN JOINING THE PHOTOGRAPHY CLUB AND WOULD LIKE TO KNOW WHAT DAY AND TIME THE CLUB MEETS EACH WEEK.
quests.hint: The club and meeting times are in the subject; the manager is addressed formally; the question covers both day and time; 'KIND REGARDS' closes the public service enquiry.
quests.explanation: Asking for both the day AND the time in one question is more efficient than two separate emails. 'Kind regards' is a universally safe and professional closing for public organisations.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write an email congratulating a friend who has been promoted at work.
options: DEAR JAMES,
SUBJECT: MASSIVE CONGRATULATIONS ON YOUR PROMOTION!

BEST WISHES,
FIONA
I WAS THRILLED TO HEAR ABOUT YOUR PROMOTION TO SENIOR MANAGER - YOU HAVE WORKED INCREDIBLY HARD AND EVERY BIT OF IT IS WELL DESERVED.
quests.hint: 'DEAR JAMES' is the warm friendly greeting; the praise in the body is sincere and specific; 'BEST WISHES' closes; the enthusiastic subject sets the celebratory tone.
quests.explanation: Using specific language like 'Senior Manager' shows you paid attention to the details of your friend's news. Saying it is 'well deserved' makes the congratulations feel personal rather than formulaic.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write an email to an online retailer requesting a refund for a damaged item.
options: DEAR CUSTOMER SERVICES,
I RECEIVED MY ORDER ON MONDAY AND UNFORTUNATELY THE ITEM WAS DAMAGED ON ARRIVAL - I WOULD LIKE TO REQUEST A FULL REFUND.
SUBJECT: REFUND REQUEST - DAMAGED ITEM ORDER #4821

YOURS FAITHFULLY,
DAWN MITCHELL
quests.hint: The order number in the subject helps customer services find your account immediately; 'DEAR CUSTOMER SERVICES' without a name requires 'YOURS FAITHFULLY'; the damage and request are in the body.
quests.explanation: Including an order number in the subject line speeds up customer service responses enormously. When writing to an unknown recipient, 'Yours faithfully' is the correct formal closing in British English.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write an email to a friend thanking them for cooking a lovely meal.
options:
WITH LOVE,
SAM
DEAR LUCY,
WHAT A WONDERFUL EVENING! THANK YOU SO MUCH FOR COOKING SUCH A DELICIOUS MEAL - THE PASTA WAS ABSOLUTELY OUTSTANDING.
SUBJECT: THANK YOU FOR THE MOST DELICIOUS DINNER
quests.hint: 'DEAR LUCY' opens warmly; 'WITH LOVE' closes affectionately between friends; the specific dish mentioned in the body makes the thanks genuine; the enthusiastic subject sets the tone.
quests.explanation: Mentioning a specific dish you enjoyed ('the pasta') demonstrates that your praise is genuine, not just polite. Starting with 'What a wonderful evening!' creates an enthusiastic, personal opening.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write an email to a teacher asking for the holiday homework details.
options: DEAR MRS COOPER,
COULD YOU PLEASE REMIND ME OF THE HOLIDAY HOMEWORK THAT WAS SET IN TODAY'S LESSON, AS I AM WORRIED I WROTE IT DOWN INCORRECTLY?

YOURS SINCERELY,
NATASHA BELL
SUBJECT: QUESTION ABOUT HOLIDAY HOMEWORK
quests.hint: The homework topic is in the subject; 'DEAR MRS COOPER' addresses the teacher formally; the honest reason ('wrote it down incorrectly') is given in the body; 'YOURS SINCERELY' closes respectfully.
quests.explanation: Being honest about why you are asking ('worried I wrote it down incorrectly') is more effective than just asking for the information. It shows self-awareness and responsibility.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write a first email to a pen pal abroad introducing yourself.
options: SUBJECT: GREETINGS FROM YOUR NEW PEN PAL IN SCOTLAND

BEST WISHES,
LIAM
DEAR ASTRID,
MY NAME IS LIAM AND I LIVE IN EDINBURGH - I ENJOY FOOTBALL AND READING AND I LOOK FORWARD TO WRITING TO YOU REGULARLY.
quests.hint: The greeting and location are in the subject; 'DEAR ASTRID' is a polite first contact; personal details and interests form the body; 'BEST WISHES' closes with warmth.
quests.explanation: A pen pal introduction should include your name, location, and a couple of interests to give your new correspondent something to respond to. 'Best wishes' is a universally friendly international closing.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write an email inviting your aunt to a birthday dinner.
options: I AM HAVING A SMALL BIRTHDAY DINNER ON FRIDAY THE 20TH AT 7 PM AND WOULD LOVE FOR YOU TO JOIN US.

WITH MUCH LOVE,
EMILY
SUBJECT: INVITATION TO MY BIRTHDAY DINNER ON FRIDAY 20TH
DEAR AUNT PATRICIA,
quests.hint: The occasion, date, and time go in the subject; 'DEAR AUNT PATRICIA' addresses family warmly; the key details are in the body; 'WITH MUCH LOVE' closes affectionately.
quests.explanation: 'With much love' is a warm family closing slightly more emphatic than 'With love'. When inviting family to a special occasion, include the date and time clearly so there is no confusion.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write an email to a sports club asking about an upcoming event.
options:
YOURS FAITHFULLY,
TYLER JAMES
DEAR EVENTS COORDINATOR,
SUBJECT: QUESTION ABOUT THE HALF-MARATHON IN OCTOBER
I AM INTERESTED IN TAKING PART IN YOUR HALF-MARATHON IN OCTOBER AND WOULD LIKE TO KNOW HOW TO REGISTER AND WHAT THE ENTRY FEE IS.
quests.hint: The event and month are in the subject; 'EVENTS COORDINATOR' names a role, not a person; the two key questions are in the body; the closing must match an unnamed greeting.
quests.explanation: Addressing someone by their job title, like 'Events Coordinator', is more precise than 'Team', but it still isn't their name - so 'Yours faithfully' is the correct closing, not 'Yours sincerely'.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write an email thanking a neighbour for helping you move house.
options:
WITH WARMEST THANKS,
THE MURPHY FAMILY
SUBJECT: THANK YOU SO MUCH FOR HELPING US MOVE
WE ARE SO GRATEFUL FOR ALL THE HELP YOU GAVE US WITH OUR MOVE LAST WEEKEND - WE COULD NOT HAVE DONE IT WITHOUT YOU.
DEAR RICHARD AND HELEN,
quests.hint: 'DEAR RICHARD AND HELEN' addresses both people; 'WITH WARMEST THANKS' expresses deep gratitude in the closing; the specific help and sentiment form the body.
quests.explanation: 'With warmest thanks' is a closing specifically suited to expressing deep gratitude. Signing as a family ('The Murphy Family') is natural when the help was given to the whole household.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write an email to a cinema asking about a specific film screening.
options: SUBJECT: QUESTION ABOUT SHOWINGS OF THE NEW SCIENCE DOCUMENTARY
DEAR CINEMA OFFICE,

MANY THANKS,
ROBERT GRAY
PLEASE COULD YOU LET ME KNOW WHEN THE NEW SCIENCE DOCUMENTARY IS BEING SHOWN AND WHETHER IT IS SUBTITLED?
quests.hint: The film type is in the subject; the office is addressed simply; two practical questions are asked in the body; 'MANY THANKS' closes the routine customer enquiry.
quests.explanation: 'Please could you let me know' is a polite, standard phrase in British English customer enquiries. Asking about subtitles alongside screening times is considerate for those who need them.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write an apology email for missing a friend's birthday dinner.
options: DEAR NINA,
I AM REALLY SORRY FOR MISSING YOUR BIRTHDAY DINNER LAST NIGHT - MY CAR BROKE DOWN AND I WAS STUCK WAITING FOR RECOVERY.
SUBJECT: I AM SO SORRY I MISSED YOUR BIRTHDAY DINNER

WITH APOLOGIES AND LOVE,
CHRIS
quests.hint: The apology is in the subject; 'DEAR NINA' opens warmly but seriously; the reason for absence is explained in the body; the combined closing shows both apology and affection.
quests.explanation: A good apology email includes a clear reason (not just an excuse) and shows genuine regret. The closing 'With apologies and love' cleverly combines the apologetic tone with the warmth appropriate between close friends.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write an email congratulating a younger relative on a great exam result.
options:
SO MUCH LOVE,
AUNT CLAIRE
WE ARE SO INCREDIBLY PROUD OF YOUR EXAM RESULTS - ALL THAT HARD WORK AND REVISION YOU PUT IN HAS CLEARLY PAID OFF.
SUBJECT: CONGRATULATIONS ON YOUR BRILLIANT EXAM RESULTS!
DEAR THEO,
quests.hint: 'DEAR THEO' addresses the young relative warmly; 'SO MUCH LOVE' is an affectionate family closing; specific acknowledgement of hard work makes the praise meaningful.
quests.explanation: Acknowledging the effort behind the results ('all that hard work and revision') is more meaningful than just praising the grades. Family closings like 'So much love' are perfectly appropriate from an aunt to a nephew or niece.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write an email to a tourist information centre asking about local attractions.
options: SUBJECT: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION ABOUT LOCAL ATTRACTIONS

KIND REGARDS,
MARTINA BANKS
DEAR TOURIST INFORMATION CENTRE,
I AM VISITING YOUR TOWN NEXT MONTH WITH MY FAMILY AND WOULD LOVE TO RECEIVE A LIST OF YOUR RECOMMENDED LOCAL ATTRACTIONS AND EVENTS.
quests.hint: The visit purpose is in the subject; the centre is addressed by role, not name; the request is in the body; 'KIND REGARDS' closes in a friendly, approachable way.
quests.explanation: A public information service like a tourist office responds well to a friendly 'Kind regards', which suits an unnamed recipient better than 'Yours sincerely'. Mentioning that you're travelling with family helps them tailor their recommendations.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write an email thanking a friend for lending you a book.
options: DEAR SOPHIE,

LOVE FROM,
NIAMH
I FINISHED THE BOOK YOU LENT ME AND I ABSOLUTELY LOVED IT - THANK YOU SO MUCH, I WILL BRING IT BACK THIS WEEK.
SUBJECT: THANK YOU FOR LENDING ME THE NOVEL
quests.hint: 'DEAR SOPHIE' opens the friendly email; 'LOVE FROM' closes casually between friends; the response to the book and the promise to return it form the body.
quests.explanation: Confirming when you will return a borrowed item ('I will bring it back this week') shows responsibility and consideration. 'Love from' is casual and suitable for a close female friendship.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write an email to a gym asking about fitness classes for beginners.
options: SUBJECT: ENQUIRY ABOUT BEGINNER FITNESS CLASSES
I AM NEW TO EXERCISE AND WOULD LIKE TO KNOW WHAT FITNESS CLASSES YOU RUN FOR BEGINNERS AND HOW I CAN BOOK A PLACE.

BEST REGARDS,
DOMINIC WALSH
DEAR PERSONAL TRAINING TEAM,
quests.hint: The target audience (beginners) is in the subject; the team is addressed by role, not name; two practical questions are in the body; 'BEST REGARDS' closes warmly and professionally.
quests.explanation: Describing yourself as 'new to exercise' immediately tells the fitness team what level to recommend. 'Best regards' is a warm, modern closing that doesn't wrongly assume you know a specific person's name.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write an email to a friend inviting them to watch a film at your house.
options: SUBJECT: FILM NIGHT AT MINE - ARE YOU FREE FRIDAY?
HI JAKE,
I AM HAVING A FILM NIGHT AT MY PLACE ON FRIDAY - WOULD YOU LIKE TO COME OVER AT ABOUT 7 PM?

SEE YOU THEN, HOPEFULLY!
CALLUM
quests.hint: 'HI JAKE' is the casual friendly opening; the playful closing reflects the informal invitation; the simple plan is in the body; the casual subject sets the fun tone.
quests.explanation: Informal emails to friends can use highly casual language throughout. A subject like 'Film night at mine' gets the message across immediately. 'See you then, hopefully!' adds a light, cheerful tone.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write an email to the local council asking about recycling services.
options:
KIND REGARDS,
SANDRA PRICE
SUBJECT: QUESTION ABOUT RECYCLING COLLECTION IN MY AREA
DEAR WASTE MANAGEMENT SERVICES,
I WOULD LIKE TO KNOW WHICH DAYS RECYCLING IS COLLECTED IN MY STREET AND WHETHER GLASS CAN BE INCLUDED IN THE KERBSIDE BOX.
quests.hint: The recycling topic is in the subject; the correct service department is addressed; two specific practical questions are in the body; 'KIND REGARDS' closes the public service enquiry.
quests.explanation: Addressing the specific department ('Waste Management Services') rather than 'the Council' in general ensures your email reaches the right team faster. Two specific questions are more helpful than a vague enquiry.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write a thank-you email for receiving a gift voucher.
options: THANK YOU SO MUCH FOR THE GIFT VOUCHER - I AM GOING TO USE IT TO BUY A NEW BOOK I HAVE HAD MY EYE ON FOR A WHILE.
DEAR UNCLE PAUL,
SUBJECT: THANK YOU FOR THE GIFT VOUCHER

WITH LOVE,
ELLA
quests.hint: 'DEAR UNCLE PAUL' opens warmly for a family member; 'WITH LOVE' closes affectionately; the plan to use the voucher shows thoughtfulness in the body.
quests.explanation: Telling the gift giver how you plan to use a voucher ('a new book I have had my eye on') makes the thank-you feel personalised rather than a generic response. It also shows that the gift will be put to good use.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write an email to a council asking about volunteering opportunities.
options:
YOURS FAITHFULLY,
BRENDA HAYES
SUBJECT: INTEREST IN VOLUNTEERING WITH THE COUNCIL
DEAR COMMUNITY SERVICES TEAM,
I AM AN ADULT LOOKING TO GIVE SOMETHING BACK TO MY COMMUNITY AND WOULD LIKE TO KNOW WHAT VOLUNTEERING ROLES YOU CURRENTLY HAVE AVAILABLE.
quests.hint: The purpose (volunteering) is in the subject; 'COMMUNITY SERVICES TEAM' names a team, not a person; the motivation and question form the body; the closing must match this unnamed greeting.
quests.explanation: Because the email is addressed to a team rather than a named individual, 'Yours faithfully' is the grammatically correct closing here, not 'Yours sincerely'. Explaining your motivation upfront often results in a more helpful reply.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write an email congratulating a friend on the birth of a new baby.
options: SUBJECT: CONGRATULATIONS ON THE ARRIVAL OF YOUR BABY!
WE WERE OVERJOYED TO HEAR THE WONDERFUL NEWS OF YOUR NEW BABY'S ARRIVAL - CONGRATULATIONS TO YOU BOTH, YOU WILL BE AMAZING PARENTS.
DEAR KATE AND TOM,

WITH LOVE AND BEST WISHES,
THE GRIFFITHS FAMILY
quests.hint: Both parents are addressed; the combined closing 'With love and best wishes' suits a very special occasion; the heartfelt message is in the body; the joyful subject sets the tone.
quests.explanation: Writing to both parents as a couple ('Kate and Tom') and signing as a whole family creates a sense of shared celebration. 'With love and best wishes' combines warmth with good wishes for the future.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write an email to a council asking about parking permits in a residential area.
options: SUBJECT: ENQUIRY ABOUT RESIDENT PARKING PERMITS
I HAVE RECENTLY MOVED TO MAPLE AVENUE AND WOULD LIKE TO KNOW HOW TO APPLY FOR A RESIDENT PARKING PERMIT FOR MY VEHICLE.

KIND REGARDS,
IAN ROSS
DEAR PARKING SERVICES TEAM,
quests.hint: The permit topic and area type are in the subject; the relevant team is addressed; the reason for enquiring and the question are in the body; 'KIND REGARDS' closes the local authority enquiry.
quests.explanation: Mentioning that you recently moved explains why you need the information now rather than before. 'Kind regards' is ideal for functional administrative enquiries like parking permits.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write a goodbye email to colleagues on your last day at a company.
options: SUBJECT: MY LAST DAY - THANK YOU ALL SO MUCH

WITH WARMEST WISHES FOR YOUR FUTURE,
AMY ROBERTS
TODAY IS MY FINAL DAY AT THE COMPANY AND I WANT TO THANK EACH OF YOU FOR THE MEMORIES, LAUGHS, AND SUPPORT OVER THE YEARS.
DEAR TEAM,
quests.hint: 'DEAR TEAM' addresses the group; the personal thanks are in the body; the warm and slightly formal closing suits a professional farewell; the subject signals this is a goodbye.
quests.explanation: 'Dear team' is a common way to address a department group in a farewell. The longer closing ('With warmest wishes for your future') adds a personal touch appropriate for a team you have worked with for years.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write an email to a local events website asking about upcoming activities.
options:
MANY THANKS,
VICKY SPENCER
SUBJECT: QUESTION ABOUT UPCOMING EVENTS IN THE LOCAL AREA
I HAVE JUST MOVED TO THE AREA AND WOULD LOVE TO KNOW ABOUT ANY UPCOMING COMMUNITY EVENTS, MARKETS, OR ACTIVITIES HAPPENING NEARBY.
DEAR EVENTS WEBSITE TEAM,
quests.hint: The general purpose is in the subject; the team is addressed simply; the reason for asking and type of event sought are in the body; 'MANY THANKS' closes the community enquiry.
quests.explanation: Explaining you have just moved justifies why you are asking about local events. Listing the types of events you are interested in ('markets, activities') helps the team give you a more tailored response.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Write an email thanking someone who provided a reference for a job application.
options:
YOURS SINCERELY,
GEORGIA BLAKE
I WANTED TO THANK YOU SINCERELY FOR AGREEING TO ACT AS MY REFERENCE - I AM DELIGHTED TO LET YOU KNOW THAT I HAVE BEEN OFFERED THE JOB.
DEAR DR HAMMOND,
SUBJECT: THANK YOU FOR PROVIDING MY REFERENCE
quests.hint: 'DEAR DR HAMMOND' uses the formal professional title; sharing the good news in the body makes the thanks more meaningful; 'YOURS SINCERELY' closes the professional correspondence.
quests.explanation: A reference thank-you email becomes much more powerful when you share the outcome ('I have been offered the job'). It lets your referee know their support made a difference. Always use the person's title when they are a doctor or professor.
